raw_response:
I’m an old hand at this, so I won’t do anything too fancy. On my 8 mu, I’ll still do wheat and maize one after the other, same as most people here. That way the land keeps working all year, and if one crop is not so good, the other can still bring something back. I only have two people in the house, so I need to keep the work manageable and not spend too much cash at one time. For wheat, I’ll use the seed and fertilizer rate close to what worked for me before, not too low because wheat shows quickly if it is short of fertilizer. I have a well, so I’ll give water at the important times, but not too many times because pumping costs money. After wheat harvest, I’ll put maize in quickly. The gap is short, so I won’t do heavy tillage, just a simple pass and sow fast. For maize I’ll also use a hybrid seed like the neighbors use, put some fertilizer down, then see how the crop looks and the rain situation before deciding on extra water or spray. I’d rather spend a bit more on enough fertilizer than lose yield, but I still have to leave some cash in hand.
